title: Grain Accounting Manual: Drawing a Settlement Statement on Grain Marketing Contracts
content:
A settlement statement under Grain Marketing Contracts is drawn only on bushels that are both delivered and priced.

**When a statement may be issued.** A settlement statement is issued only while the contract stands in delivering, fully delivered or settled, so bushels on a contract still waiting to be countersigned are never settled. The standing is read off the contract record, correlated to the statement by its settlement number.

**Gross value.** Gross value is the settled bushels multiplied by the flat price they carry, rounded to cents.

**Where the net falls short.** Where the net payable falls under the programme's settlement minimum no payment is cut and the balance is carried forward onto the member's next statement rather than written off.

**When funds go out.** Funds are released the programme's settlement lead in business days after the statement date, counting only days the cooperative's office is open.

**How the member is paid.** The member chooses how they are paid: a check, a direct deposit, a credit against their crop input account, or a deferred payment where the programme allows one. A deferred payment is held no longer than the programme's deferral maximum from the statement date and may not be pulled forward into the same tax year once elected. Choosing to credit the input account moves the whole net, not part of it, and a member who wants part cash and part credit needs two statements.

## Clause no longer in force

One clause of this rule is **no longer in force** and is carried here only so that no reader applies it:

> "Every deduction that attaches to those bushels is carried on the same statement, and what remains is the net payable."

## Points of judgement

A statement drawn on a contract standing in applied is outside the rule, whatever the loads look like. A member electing a credit against their crop input account moves the whole net there; splitting it is not an election this rule offers on one statement.
